correctness.rationale: Exact harmonic-mode norm calculation yields the Fourier coefficients; reciprocal decomposition gives the Poisson mixture. The normalized quotient has strictly positive angular derivative and strictly negative radial derivative at opposite angles. Together with a positive same-direction endpoint they prove a unique first zero radius and exactly two zeros on each larger circle. Nonzero gradients make one embedded analytic arc. Uniform coefficient convergence and dominated convergence prove the two endpoint constants. The packaged checker verifies representative formulas and sign changes but is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The all-parameter zero-set topology for a canonical Hilbert norm interpolation is a structural classification: the maximal zero-free product disk is sharp, exactly one connected nonsingular nodal curve persists for every finite boundary penalty, and the large-penalty limit has a specific nontrivial asymptotic constant. These consequences distinguish harmonic from holomorphic stabilization and are not merely isolated computed roots.
